Further, aggrieved by the said order, the Petitioner approached the Hon’ble Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (in short, ‘APTEL’) and preferred an appeal bearing No. 113 of 2024. The Petitioner has also filed an Appeal No. 411 of 2023 before APTEL assailing the Tariff order dated 28.10.2019 in Petition 43/GT/2018 (C.O.D to 31.03.2019). The Petitioner has sought indulgence to consider the outcome of Appeal Nos. 113/2024 and 411 of 2023 at the time of truing-up of tariff for the period 2019-24 and while determining the tariff for the period 2024-29. Pertinently, the said appeals are pending; any impact of the same shall be considered as and when the same is decided by APTEL. 4. The Petitioner, in terms of Regulation 13 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, has filed the present petition for the true-up of the tariff, based on the actual capital expenditure incurred for the period 2019-2024. The Petitioner, in response to the Commission’s technical validation (TV) letter, has furnished the additional information, vide affidavit dated 2.7.2025. The Respondents, UPPCL and CSPDCL, have filed their replies vide affidavit dated 12.9.2025 and 21.7.2025, respectively, and the Petitioner has filed its rejoinder to the said replies. The same has been considered for tariff purposes. The summary of claims made by the Petitioner and allowed by the Commission for the 2019-24 period is as under: 52. The Petitioner has claimed the impact of Goods and Services Tax given as under: The annual fixed charges claimed by the Petitioner vide affidavit dated 2.7.2025 in _(a) Payment made against award of arbitration or for compliance with the directions or order of any statutory authority, or order or decree of any court of law;_ _(a) Payment made against award of arbitration or for compliance of order or directions of any statutory authority, or order or decree of any court of law;_ 91. The Petitioner has submitted that a dispute has arisen with the contractor M/s Hindustan Construction Company (HCC), wherein the HCC, before the Arbitral Tribunal, has claimed additional cost for extension of time, for losses suffered and a claim for payment of interest on invoices wrongfully withheld by the Petitioner. The Arbitral Tribunal, vide its order dated 14.10.2019 (corrected on 7.3.2020), awarded an amount of Rs. 11687.00 lakh (Principal), Rs. 8.70 lakh (Stamp duty and expenses on data programming) and interest amount of Rs. 4668.00 lakh @ 12% p.a. from 20.5.2016 till the date of award and 9% from the date of award till the date of actual payment in favour of HCC. The Petitioner has further submitted that the award passed by the Arbitral Tribunal was challenged before the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi, and the Petitioner, in compliance with the direction of the court, has deposited Rs. 16355.00 lakh (principal of Rs 11687.00 lakh plus interest Rs 4668.00 lakh) with the Registrar General of the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi on 8.10.2020. In view of the same, the Petitioner has claimed Rs. 11687.00 lakh (principal amount) under Regulation 25(1)(a) as additional capital expenditure for 2024-25 and has prayed for reimbursement of Rs. 4668.00 lakh (interest amount) under Regulation 91 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. Additionally, the Petitioner has claimed Rs. 6274.00 lakh as strictly in terms of the Tariff Regulations, after accounting for DSM and secondary response adjustments, and reconciling the data with the final REA. Considering the fact that the present petition is for truing-up of tariff of the generating station for the period 2019-24, we find no reason to consider the claims towards the recovery of the shortfall in energy charges in this petition, However, the parties are at liberty to agitate the same by way of a separate petition and the same will be considered in accordance with law. 134. The Petitioner has sought reimbursement of fees paid by it for filing the petition and for publication expenses and has submitted that the reimbursement of the same is in accordance in terms of the Regulation 94 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. In view of the above, the Petitioner shall be entitled to the reimbursement of the filing fees and publication expenses in connection with the filing of this petition, directly from the beneficiaries, on a pro rata basis, in accordance with Regulation 94 of the 2024 Tariff Regulation.
